source_spans.locator: Nature Neuroscience 5, published p.1226, Abstract: stochastic optimal feedback control permits variability in redundant dimensions and corrects deviations selectively when they interfere with task goals

Nature Neuroscience 5, published p.1227, optimal-control assumptions: feedback law chosen for the task; delayed/noisy sensory access; internal forward model estimates current state from feedback, plant dynamics, and prior control signals

Nature Neuroscience 5, published pp.1228-1229, minimal-intervention result and formalization: redundant deviations need not trigger correction; feedback law minimizes expected cumulative task/effort cost and correction covaries with cost-to-go change

Nature Neuroscience 5, published p.1233, external-perturbation discussion and Sim 9: random perturbation to control signals produces large changes in an intermediate trajectory while the task-relevant end-effector trajectory rapidly returns to the target sinusoid

conditions: the task admits redundant solutions, movement duration exceeds the shortest sensorimotor delay, and either the initial plant state or the consequences of control signals are uncertain
task performance is evaluated by an expected cost that includes task error and effort
population: motor-control systems treated at the computational level, with human movement experiments and simulations used to test the theory
task: achieve task-level movement goals under redundancy and uncertainty while limiting expected task error and control effort
temporal_scope: a time-varying feedback law selects controls moment-by-moment during movement from a current state estimate built from delayed/noisy sensory feedback, plant dynamics, and prior control signals

nodes.description: current plant-state estimate available to the controller, formed by integrating delayed noisy sensory feedback with plant dynamics and prior control signals
time-varying mapping from estimated state and time to control actions that minimizes expected cumulative cost for the task
deviation that changes task performance or expected cost-to-go
redundant deviation that does not change task performance or expected cost-to-go
control action produced by the feedback policy in response to the estimated current state
expected cumulative objective combining task error with an effort penalty on control
source simulation in which random perturbations are added to control signals to compare resistance in task-relevant versus redundant movement dimensions

relations.description: the feedback policy uses the current state estimate to select the control action appropriate to the current circumstances

under the minimal-intervention relation, deviations that interfere with task performance are corrected, whereas strictly redundant deviations can receive no corrective action and are allowed greater variability
the policy is defined by minimizing expected cumulative task and effort cost under stochastic dynamics

the source's perturbation simulation distinguishes selective correction: the task-relevant end-effector trajectory rapidly returns to target while a redundant intermediate trajectory can change substantially
